author: Bechstein, 1803
summary: 전국에서 볼 수 있으나 흔하지 않은 텃새로, 낙엽활엽수림이나 아고산대의 침엽수와 활엽수가 섞인 숲에 산다. 홀로 또는 암수가 함께 지내며, 나무줄기에 손수 구멍을 뚫어 둥지로 쓴다. 4월 하순부터 한배에 알 3~5개를 낳는다. 곤충을 주로 먹고 다족류와 여러 식물의 열매도 먹는다.

art.subject: White-backed Woodpecker (Dendrocopos leucotos), adult male, as seen in Korean deciduous forest in spring: crown and nape entirely bright red; narrow forehead buffy white; face and ear coverts buffy white, bordered below by a black moustachial stripe from the bill base that continues into black streaks on the breast sides; chin and throat whitish with a faint rusty-yellow wash; mantle black; lower back white; wings black with bold white bars across coverts and flight feathers, no white shoulder patch; underparts buffy white with black streaks on the breast sides and flanks, turning pinkish-red on the lower belly and undertail coverts. Bill lead-grey. Red-brown iris. Dark lead-grey legs.
art.pose: clinging to a tree trunk, chiselling out a nest hole with its bill
art.scene: Korean deciduous broadleaf forest grading into subalpine mixed conifer-broadleaf woods in spring; no people, buildings or text
views: adult male, side view clinging upright to a trunk: all-red crown and nape, buff-white face with black moustachial stripe, black back, white-barred black wings, black-streaked flanks, pinkish-red vent, long lead-grey bill, dark grey legs
adult female, head detail in profile: black crown and nape with no red, buff-white forehead and face, black moustachial line, whitish throat washed rusty-yellow
art.build: Large pied woodpecker, 25–28cm, clearly bigger and longer-billed than Great Spotted Woodpecker, about the length of a Brown-eared Bulbul but much stockier. Bill long, straight and chisel-tipped, lead-grey, about as long as the head. Legs short, dark grey, two toes forward and two back; clings upright to trunks propped on its stiff, pointed black tail. Wings black, barred white in rows; no white oval shoulder patch. In flight undulating, showing the white lower back.
avoid: Do not paint a large white oval shoulder patch or clean unstreaked underparts — that is Great Spotted Woodpecker (Dendrocopos major).
Do not restrict the male's red to a small nape spot; the whole crown is red.
Do not paint a sharply defined scarlet vent; the red is pinkish and blends into the streaked flanks.
Do not give the female any red on the head.
